originalTitle: Australia news live: Israel ambassador insists IDF strike that killed Zomi Frankcom a ‘reasonable mistake’; body of hiker Lily Hooper recovered from bush
content: Sydney air traffic controllers have ‘grave concerns’ about collision risk after airspace redesign Air traffic controllers at Sydney airport have warned federal safety regulators they have “grave concerns” about changes to airspace rules introduced last month, likening the situation to the months leading up to a crash in Washington DC in which 67 people died. Guardian Australia can reveal the federal government was notified on Thursday of a confidential complaint considered by the Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB), in which an experienced air traffic controller warned in June that changes related to the new Western Sydney International airport had been rushed, with “inadequate training for controllers, of all experience levels”. The complainant told the regulator a large group of controllers in Sydney “hold grave concerns about the project”, referring to the air traffic redesign to accommodate the new airport. Read more: Brisbane woman allegedly attacked and raped on morning walk A man has been charged with several counts of rape after an alleged random attack on a woman who was out on a morning walk, AAP reports. The woman, aged in her 20s, was walking in the leafy, semi-rural Brisbane suburb of Brookfield around 6.30am on Thursday when she was allegedly stopped by an unknown man, police said in a statement. The man allegedly sexually assaulted the victim multiple times before he fled the scene on foot. Police later arrested a 32-year-old man a short distance from the scene. He has been charged with six counts of rape, stalking, assault with intent to commit rape, assault occasioning bodily harm and deprivation of liberty. He is due to appear in court later today. Police said while the attack was being treated as an isolated incident, police patrols would be increased in the Brookfield area over the coming days. Woman behind allegation of sexual assault linked to Sydney Swans reportedly says she wants ‘justice’ The woman who alleges she was sexually assaulted in a Melbourne hotel told the Herald Sun “all I care about is justice”. Police are investigating the alleged assault, which is linked to a night out that resulted in five Swans players being suspended for the rest of the AFL season for breaching club standards. The players reportedly returned to the hotel in the early hours of Monday morning after drinking, following the victory over Essendon at the MCG that secured the Swans a home final. None have been arrested or charged, but police are continuing their investigations. The Guardian does not suggest that any of the players are being accused of sexual assault, and it is reported that none of the banned players has been formally interviewed by police. The five players released a statement on Wednesday saying they are “deeply sorry” after the suspension – which came after an independent investigation by the Swans organisation – for the breach of standards following a night of drinking, saying their behaviour had fallen “well short of the standards expected of us and the values of our Club”. The apology did not mention the allegations of assault and there is no suggestion they are related. The players said their focus would “now be on rebuilding trust with the Club and the community”. The woman, who was not identified by the Herald Sun, told the outlet she was hired to perform lap dances at the Melbourne hotel. She said up there were about nine men in the room who told her and another dancer they were tradies. She said she could not provide detail about the alleged incident, but told the paper: I don’t want money. All I care about is justice. I’m going to stand up for what is right. And I’m never going to let this happen to anyone else. Justice will be served. The body of missing bushwalker Lily Hooper has been recovered from NSW southern highlands overnight, NSW police confirmed. The confirmation comes after widespread confusion on Thursday when police wrongly reported to the 18-year-old’s parents, the New South Wales premier and the media that the missing bushwalker had been found alive. Hooper had last been seen on 12 August after leaving home for a hike in the rugged bushland of Nattai national park, 90km south-west of Sydney. She was reported missing that night, triggering a multi-agency search involving nearly 1,000 people, including hundreds of volunteers. A police spokesperson confirmed on Friday morning that the body of a woman believed to be Hooper was winched out of the area on Thursday night. Hillel Newman, the Israeli ambassador to Australia, maintained the IDF attack on an aid convoy that killed Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom was a “reasonable mistake” and said disciplinary measures had been taken against IDF personnel involved. Newman spoke to RN Breakfast after the Australian government said it was “outraged” there would be no criminal investigation into Frankcom’s death. The ambassador said there were still legal processes in the appeal system that could be used as Israel is a “robust” democracy. We do grieve on the situation with the family. This was unintentional … and not deliberate in any way. … You know there are tragic circumstances in a war zone. And we’re very sorry for the family, but that does not always mean that there’s criminal liability. Butler says Israeli government should ‘demonstrate some accountability’ on Zomi Frankcom Health minister Mark Butler said the Israeli government could “demonstrate some accountability” after the country’s ambassador, Hillel Newman, was called in for formal talks following the decision not to open a criminal investigation into the death of Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom. Butler spoke to Radio National Breakfast after foreign minister Penny Wong said Australia was “outraged” after Israel announced the news. The health minister said this morning: Something monumentally bad has happened here, and it just appears there’s no accountability on that side. chineseContent: 空域重新设计后，悉尼空中交通管制员对碰撞风险表示“严重担忧” 悉尼机场的空中交通管制员警告联邦安全监管机构，他们对上个月引入的空域规则的变化表示“严重担忧”，并将这种情况比作华盛顿特区坠机事故前几个月的情况，导致 67 人死亡。 《澳大利亚卫报》透露，周四，联邦政府接到澳大利亚运输安全局 (ATSB) 审议的一份机密投诉通知，一名经验丰富的空中交通管制员在 6 月份警告说，与新西悉尼国际机场相关的改革过于仓促，“对所有经验水平的管制员都没有进行充分的培训”。投诉人告诉监管机构，悉尼的一大群管制员“对该项目表示严重担忧”，指的是为适应新机场而进行的空中交通重新设计。阅读更多：布里斯班女子涉嫌在晨间散步时遭到袭击和强奸 据澳大利亚联合社报道，一名男子因涉嫌随机袭击一名晨间散步的女子而被指控犯有多项强奸罪。警方在一份声明中称，周四早上 6 点 30 分左右，这名 20 多岁的女子在绿树成荫的布里斯班郊区布鲁克菲尔德散步，据称被一名身份不明的男子拦住。据称，该男子对受害者进行了多次性侵犯，然后步行逃离现场。警方随后在距离现场不远的地方逮捕了一名 32 岁男子。他被指控犯有六项强奸、跟踪、意图强奸、袭击导致身体伤害和剥夺自由等罪名。他定于今天晚些时候出庭。警方表示，虽然这起袭击事件被视为孤立事件，但警方将加强巡逻
